data.title: Efalizumab & alefacept (withdrawn T-cell biologics)
data.summary: Biologicals · T-cell targeted biologics for psoriasis — efalizumab (anti-CD11a monoclonal) and alefacept (LFA-3/IgG1 fusion protein)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Biologicals_

**Class:** T-cell targeted biologics for psoriasis — efalizumab (anti-CD11a monoclonal) and alefacept (LFA-3/IgG1 fusion protein)

## Mechanism of action
- Efalizumab: blocks CD11a (LFA-1) → prevents T-cell activation and migration into skin
- Alefacept: binds CD2 on memory T cells → blocks LFA-3/CD2 co-stimulation and causes NK-mediated apoptosis of CD45RO+ memory T cells

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Formerly: moderate–severe chronic plaque psoriasis
- Efalizumab withdrawn in 2009 (progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy); alefacept withdrawn in 2011 (commercial reasons/low efficacy)

## Dose & formulations
- Historic: efalizumab 1 mg/kg SC weekly; alefacept 15 mg IM weekly × 12 weeks (needed CD4 count monitoring)

## Adverse effects
- Efalizumab: PML (JC virus), rebound/flare of psoriasis on stopping, thrombocytopenia, aseptic meningitis
- Alefacept: CD4 lymphopenia, infections, malignancy concerns

## Contraindications
- No longer marketed

## Pregnancy & lactation
Not applicable (withdrawn).

## Viva points
- Efalizumab withdrawn due to PML
- Alefacept — first biologic approved for psoriasis (2003); depletes memory T cells; CD4 monitoring

_Sources: Khopkar (Immunobiologicals — efalizumab, alefacept); Wolverton 4e ch.8 (Drugs taken off the market). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
